title: Collab: shapes drawn by one user intermittently not synced to others (data loss)
description:
SEVERITY: HIGH — silent collaborative DATA LOSS / corruption. A shape drawn by peer A is
intermittently not seen (or seen duplicated, or with wrong z-order) by peer B during live
two-peer editing. Reproduced in-process; root-caused to a non-CRDT-safe order-array rewrite.

== SYMPTOM ==
Real user report: occasionally a shape drawn by user A is NOT seen by user B (intermittent).
Manifests as a missing shape, a duplicated shape neither user drew, or scrambled z-order on
a keyframe that two peers edited near-simultaneously.

== REPRODUCED (JOB 1) ==
Scratch tests in packages/collab/src/__tests__ (removed after): two FlashCollabBindings over
an ASYNCHRONOUS loopback wire (buffered updates, flushed on demand — modeling real network
latency, NOT the synchronous loopback the existing property/binding tests use). Peer A draws
shapes through the REAL merge-on-commit path (setKeyframeDisplayObjects -> store REPLACE,
mirroring collabAdapter's pushDoc->REPLACE downgrade). Failing sequence:
  1. B draws shape B1; flush B->A   (A.lastSynced now = [B1], __order=[B1])
  2. A draws A1, A2 locally           (A.__order=[B1,A1,A2])
  3. B draws B2 concurrently
  4. flush all
  => FINAL __order on BOTH ydocs = [B1, B2, B1, A1, A2]  <-- "B1" DUPLICATED
     keyed Y.Map entries are CORRECT (B1,B2,A1,A2 each once) but __order is corrupt.
  rebuildKeyed walks __order -> emits B1 twice -> rebuilt display list has a duplicate id
  and the wrong length; downstream REPLACE diffs de-dup the id, dropping a real shape.

The DETERMINISTIC, SYNCHRONOUS reproductions (rapid successive draws; draw+immediate second
mutation; even synchronous concurrent A/B draws; re-entrant draw during applyRemote) ALL
PASS — which is exactly why the existing P0 property test (7200 deterministic mutations,
synchronous wire) never caught it. The bug needs CONCURRENT edits to the SAME keyed
container with ASYNC (buffered) delivery so both peers' order rewrites are genuinely
concurrent CRDT ops.

Minimal CRDT-primitive proof (200/200 trials corrupt): two Y.Docs sharing order=[S0]; each
appends one id via delete(0,len)+insert(0,newArr) concurrently; after merge BOTH converge to
[S0, A, S0, B] — the pre-existing S0 duplicated, 100% of the time.

== ROOT CAUSE (JOB 2) — candidate (a)/(e): non-CRDT-safe whole-array __order rewrite ==
packages/collab/src/schema.ts, reconcileKeyed(), lines 206-212:

    const desired = next.map((i) => i.id);
    const current = order.toArray();
    if (!arraysEqual(current, desired)) {
      if (current.length > 0) order.delete(0, current.length);  // delete ALL
      if (desired.length > 0) order.insert(0, desired);         // insert ALL at 0
    }

The keyed-container "__order" Y.Array (which records display-object / library-item order)
is reconciled by DELETING THE WHOLE ARRAY and RE-INSERTING the whole desired sequence at
index 0 on EVERY change — even a single append (arraysEqual is false for any append, so the
fast path never applies). Y.Array delete+insert are CRDT ops: when two peers each do this
concurrently, peer A's delete only removes the elements A observed, NOT B's concurrently-
inserted ids, and both peers' insert(0, ...) survive and interleave. Result: duplicated
and/or mis-ordered ids in __order that BOTH peers converge to (so it is not a divergence —
it is convergent CORRUPTION). rebuildKeyed (schema.ts:215-233) reads the id sequence from
__order, so a duplicate id => a duplicate display object; an interleave that drops a real id
=> that shape is silently absent from the rebuilt FlashDocument (the user-reported "shape not
seen"). The keyed Y.Map ENTRIES are fine; only the order index is corrupt.

WHY INTERMITTENT: it requires two peers to mutate the SAME keyed container (same keyframe's
displayObjects, or the library items map) within the same async/network window so their
order-array rewrites are concurrent (not causally ordered). Solo, sequential, or
synchronously-serialized edits never collide — the delete+insert is then causally ordered
and behaves like a clean replace. Hence it shows up only under live concurrent drawing and
is invisible to single-peer use and to the synchronous deterministic property test.

This same defective pattern is used in THREE places, all with identical risk:
  - reconcileKeyed __order rewrite (schema.ts:206-212)   -> displayObjects, library items
  - reconcileAsClasses __order rewrite (schema.ts:549-554) -> asClasses
  - setPlainArray whole-array rewrite (schema.ts:262-266)  -> classpaths/publishProfiles/folders
(setPlainArray is lower risk: those arrays change rarely and are usually edited by one peer,
but the same concurrent-rewrite corruption applies.)

== SCOPE / SEVERITY (JOB 3) ==
- NOT specific to shapes: reconcileKeyed handles BOTH frame displayObjects AND library items,
  so concurrent library adds (e.g. two peers importing/creating symbols) corrupt the library
  __order identically. Text/instances ARE display objects too — any concurrent edit to the
  same keyframe's object set is affected, shapes are just the most common interactive case.
- NOT the REPLACE path per se: the REPLACE (whole-array setKeyframeDisplayObjects) MAXIMIZES
  exposure because every commit triggers a full __order rewrite, but the root cause is the
  order-array reconciliation strategy, not REPLACE vs incremental.
- Severity HIGH: silent, convergent data corruption (duplicate/missing/reordered objects) in
  the core collaborative drawing flow, with no error surfaced to either user.

== FIX DIRECTION ==
Make the __order reconciliation a MINIMAL, position-stable CRDT edit instead of delete-all+
insert-all. Options, preferred first:
  1. Diff current vs desired and emit only the minimal inserts/deletes (e.g. an LCS / longest-
     common-subsequence based splice) so an append is a single order.insert at the tail and a
     reorder touches only moved ids. Concurrent appends then commute (each peer inserts only
     its OWN new id) and no pre-existing id is ever deleted+re-inserted.
  2. Stop storing order as a Y.Array of ids entirely: give each keyed child an explicit
     fractional/lexicographic order key (a sort field on the child Y.Map) and rebuild by
     sorting — no shared positional array to corrupt. This is the most robust against
     concurrent reorder but a larger change.
  3. At minimum, dedup + drop-unknown when reading __order in rebuildKeyed AND fall back to
     container.keys() for any keyed entry MISSING from __order, so a corrupt order can never
     duplicate or DROP an object (defense-in-depth even with fix 1/2). Apply the same to
     rebuildAsClasses.
Apply the chosen fix to reconcileKeyed, reconcileAsClasses, and (lower priority) setPlainArray.

== GAP vs EXISTING VERIFICATION ==
The P0 "binding converges" property test (packages/collab/src/__tests__/property.test.ts,
7200 deterministic mutations) drives a SINGLE source over a SYNCHRONOUS wire, so every
mutation is causally ordered before the next — it can never produce two concurrent rewrites
of the same order array. The real interactive/concurrent commit path with async network
delivery does. A regression test must: bind TWO peers, deliver updates ASYNCHRONOUSLY
(buffered), have BOTH draw on the SAME keyframe concurrently, then assert each rebuilt doc's
displayObjects has exactly the union of drawn ids with NO duplicates and NO missing ids
(repeat across many interleavings/seeds).

Root cause one-liner: reconcileKeyed rewrites the entire "__order" Y.Array via
delete-all+insert-all on every change (schema.ts:206-212); two concurrent rewrites of the
same order array merge into a duplicated/garbled id sequence, and rebuildKeyed reads order
from that array, so a concurrently-drawn shape is silently duplicated or dropped.
